### Necessary packages

```{r}
# For Analysis
library(traitheritage)

# For data wrangling
library(dplyr)
```

In this paper we set out new formulations for calculating the probability of phylogenetic coalescence within and between individuals that hold a particular trait - in our case that is a linguistic trait. This document outlines those formulations mathematically and logically, with coded examples.

The probability is always calculated at a particular time-horizon, t, which we then calculate across the phylogeny to understand the trend of coalescence over the life of the phylogeny.

We also will follow the same data through this document, to act as an example.

```{r}
# Build a tree with three sets of five polytomies
tree = ape::read.tree(text = "((t1, t2, t3, t4, t5),
                                (t6, t7, t8, t9, t10),
                                (t11, t12, t13, t14, t15));")
tree = ape::compute.brlen(tree)

# Traits can be a, b, or c
# trait = factor(c("a", "a", "a", "b", "c", "b", "b", "a", "c", "c", "a", "b", "a", "b", "c"))
trait = factor(c("a", "a", "a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c", "c", "c"))
# trait = factor(c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "a", "b", "c", "d", "e"))
trait_levels = levels(trait)
names(trait) = tree$tip.label
my_colours = c(a = "#4757E8", b = "#10C378", c = "#EB9DFF")

# Plot the tree
plot(tree, tip.color = my_colours[trait])
abline(v = 0.5, col = "red", lty = "dashed")
legend("top", legend = names(my_colours), col = my_colours, pch = 19, horiz = TRUE)

```

For this document, we will have two time-horizons, which are determined by cutting the phylogeny in half (indicated by the red dashed line), resulting in three separate polytomies, or treating the whole phylogeny as a single clade.

```{r}
clades = phyloregion::get_clades(tree, cut = 0.5)
clade_traits = t(sapply(clades, function(cc) trait[cc]))
```

### Within Group variance

For all clades at a particular time-horizon, the within group probability is calculated as the sum of individuals sharing a trait, divided by the sum of possible pairs.

$$
\frac{\sum_{c=1}^{k}(\sum_{i \neq j} i = j)}{\sum_{c=1}^{k}}
$$

Below is coded example:

```{r}
### Numerator: Number of observed, within clade pairs of traits 

# The count of each trait within each clade
counts = apply(clade_traits, 1, function(ct) table(factor(ct, levels = trait_levels)))
# The number of observed pairs in each clade, summed across clades
op = apply(counts, 1, function(cnts) choose(cnts, 2)) %>% 
  colSums()

# Then do this (cant remember why)
# ppp = combn(op, 2, sum)

## Denominator:: Number of possible pairs across clades

## Number of possible pairs across all clades
tc = table(trait) # count of traits
# tp = combn(tc, 2, sum)
tp = choose(tc, 2)

## Within group Variability
(v_within = op / tp)

```

### Between Group variance

```{r}
# Numerator: number of observed dissimilar pairs within each clade, summed
crossed_clades = apply(clade_traits, 1, function(ct){
  # Trait count
  tc = table(factor(ct, levels = trait_levels)) 
  v = combn(tc, 2, FUN = prod)
  nmes = combn(names(tc), 2, FUN=paste, collapse='')
  names(v) = nmes
  v
})
numerator = rowSums(crossed_clades)

# Denominator
# count all traits
cats = table(trait)
# Number of possible dissimilar pairs across clades 
denominator = combn(cats, 2, FUN = Reduce, f = "*")
names(denominator) = combn(names(cats), 2, FUN=paste, collapse='')

(v_between = numerator / denominator)
names(v_between) = combn(names(cats), 2, FUN=paste, collapse='')
```

### Total variance

```{r}

# A & B
T = (op["a"] + op["b"] + numerator["ab"]) / (tp["a"] + tp["b"] + denominator["ab"])

# FST 
# (T - v_within["ab"]) / T
(T - (v_within["a"] + v_within["b"])) / T

## Odds Ratio
((op["a"] + op["b"]) / (tp["a"] + tp["b"])) / (numerator["ab"] / denominator["ab"])

# Product
((op["a"] + op["b"]) / numerator["ab"]) * ((tp["a"] + tp["b"]) / denominator["ab"])

# ? 
((op["a"] + op["b"]) / (tp["a"] + tp["b"])) / T




```

### FST Approximation

```{r}
(v_between - v_within) / v_between
```

### Notes

-   Simpson's Diversity: $D = 1 - \frac{\sum n (n - 1)}{N (N -1)}$
